title: Asia Week New York announces a spectacular fall line-up of gallery exhibitions
summary: An abundant array of Asian Art treasures will be offered when the Autumn 2026 Edition of Asia Week New York opens on September 10 and runs through September 18. With over a dozen New York gallery and online exhibitions combined with fall auction sales at Bonhams, Christie’s, Doyle, Freeman’s, Heritage Auctions and Sotheby’s, the week promises to be a destination for Asian art collectors and enthusiasts alike. “We’re delighted to present our capsule Autumn 2026 edition of Asia Week New York,” says Margi Gristina, chairman of Asia Week New York. “Our participants never cease to capture the diversity and essence of the field.” Alisan Fine Arts celebrates 45 years of championing contemporary Chinese art in 2026, and Chao Chung-hsiang has been a vital part of the gallery’s history since their early days. title: Oleg Prokofiev's unearthed music-inspired graphic paintings go on display in London
summary: Nearly 60 years after Oleg Prokofiev left the Soviet Union, where the abstract style in which he worked was forbidden by the state, previously unseen music-inspired graphic paintings by the artist are to go on show in London — continuing a remarkable three-generation artistic story that stretches from Sergei Prokofiev ’s 20th-century musical legacy to the contemporary work of his grandson, composer Gabriel Prokofiev. Gabriel Prokofiev, son of Oleg and grandson of Sergei Prokofiev said: “My father wasn’t a musician, instead he used the medium of painting and sculpture to express the musicality that’s flowed through our family. So much of my father’s work was hidden from public view for decades as it was in an abstract style that was forbidden by the Soviet state. title: The Stork Club, Walter Winchell & other ephemera come to Turner Auctions + Appraisals on September 12
summary: Turner Auctions + Appraisals is pleased to present Ephemera from the Stork Club, Walter Winchell & More on Saturday, September 12, 2026, at 10:30 am PDT. Much of the auction comes from Harold A. Layer, Professor Emeritus (retired) at San Francisco State University. Among these lots are his collections of the Stork Club and Walter Winchell, and two lots of card and board games/prototypes by Mr. Layer. Other auction sources include the SFO Museum for San Francisco photos and ephemera, San Francisco’s Cliff House for signed celebrity photos, and other collections and estates. Walter Winchell (1897-1972) was a famous American newspaper gossip columnist and radio commentator who invented modern celebrity journalism. title: Mount Holyoke College Art Museum reopens on September 8th after major renovation with reimagined collection galleries
summary: Mount Holyoke College Art Museum (MHCAM) will reopen to the public on September 8, 2026, following a nine-month closure for the comprehensive renovation and reinstallation of its permanent collection galleries. MHCAM at 150: Our New Collection Galleries is timed to coincide with the Museum’s 150th anniversary later this fall. The reopening marks a transformative moment in the institution’s history—one that honors its distinguished legacy while advancing a more expansive and inclusive vision of art history. title: Marijana Schneider appointed artistic director of TAXISPALAIS Kunsthalle Tirol
summary: Starting on January 4, 2027, Marijana Schneider, who was born in Germany in 1983, will hold the position of artistic director of the TAXISPALAIS Kunsthalle Tirol in Innsbruck. She will succeed Nina Tabassomi, who has served as managing and artistic director of the TAXISPALAIS since 2017 and whose tenure runs through the end of 2026. As an art historian and curator, Marijana Schneider brings along many years of practical experience in the international art and exhibition scene as well as institutional knowledge. She stands for a program that connects international contemporary art with the local art scene. “With Marijana Schneider, Tyrol gains an experienced curator and a fascinating voice in the field of contemporary art. The TAXISPALAIS, as a state gallery, is a central location of contemporary art with a decades-long tradition and international renown. title: Colnaghi London opens Out of the Sand exhibition on ancient Egypt
summary: Colnaghi London announces Out of the Sand: Ancient Egypt Rediscovered, a major exhibition bringing together ancient Egyptian artefacts with nineteenth- and early twentieth-century paintings, drawings, rare books and photographs to examine how Egypt was made, buried, recovered and repeatedly reimagined. On view through 17 November 2026, the exhibition spans some four millennia and sets objects made by ancient Egyptian hands beside the works produced by later artists, travellers, scholars and photographers who sought to record and interpret the civilisation they encountered. The exhibition takes its title from the recurring history of Egypt's rediscovery. title: Art Institute of Chicago presents Mary Cassatt: After Impressionism exhibition
summary: The Art Institute of Chicago is presenting Mary Cassatt: After Impressionism, on view September 6, 2026 through January 3, 2027. The exhibition provides a focused look at the crucial moment in Cassatt’s career from the late 1880s to the early 1900s when this relentless experimenter took her art making in new directions. During these pivotal years, Cassatt elevated her signature subject of women and children, exploring modernist aesthetics in series and across media. She centered modern women’s everyday lives in her art, making visible their intellectual and cultural pursuits in the larger world. Such vibrant portrayals are among Cassatt’s most celebrated compositions in her own time and today. title: Manship Artists Residency presents David Hockney exhibition on image reproduction
summary: Manship Artists Residency will present Hockney Reproduction(s), an exhibition examining one of the most influential artists of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, David Hockney (1937-2026), through a lens rarely given sustained attention: his lifelong engagement with the reproduction of his own imagery. The exhibition explores Hockney’s six-decade fascination with reproducing, reimaging, transmitting, and sharing his work through emerging technologies. With prints, books, multi-page faxed works, photographs, and more than 75 posters, the show reveals how reproduction served as a central force that shaped the artist’s practice. “I’ve always been interested in printing as a medium, and also as a medium through which my work can be known—can reach a public. title: Nate Lowman debuts new series of key-shaped paintings at David Zwirner
summary: David Zwirner will present new work by Nate Lowman (b. 1979), opening at the gallery’s 519 West 19th Street location in New York. The exhibition debuts a body of shaped canvases that take the form of keys–objects freighted with associations of access, security, and exclusion–a new motif for the artist. Lowman has frequently employed universally recognizable shaped canvases including hearts, tree-shaped air fresheners, poppies, and maps, among others, each produced in iterations with distinct painted surfaces. His key paintings extend this vocabulary, ranging from tightly rendered replicas to more schematic, nearly abstract forms. Some reproduce dissonant photographic imagery taken by the artist; others appropriate the bright, patterned novelty finishes available at hardware stores to distinguish one key from another; whereas another work, a silkscreen diptych, represents two keys yet to be cut into their final shape. title: Artcurial announces fall auction season featuring major private collections
summary: This season, Artcurial shines a light on a selection of private collections, each telling a singular story, shaped over time with patience, discernment and intuition. Each sale offers a rare opportunity to discover carefully selected works, where history, taste and legacy come together. To build a collection is to refine a vision and give lasting form to a passion. This season, Artcurial shines a light on a selection of private ensembles, each telling a singular story shaped by patience, discernment and intuition. Each sale offers a rare opportunity to discover carefully chosen pieces, where history, taste and legacy converge. Shaped by extensive travels throughout Africa and enriched by exchanges with leading specialists, the Jean-Jacques Rotthier Collection (Brussels, 1932-2009), assembled from the 1970s onwards, stands in the tradition of the great private collections of African art formed during the 20th century. title: RM Sotheby's marks 20 years at Hershey, led by Duesenberg Model J, Auburn 851 Speedster, and Brass Era Mercedes
summary: RM Sotheby’s returns to Hershey, Pennsylvania, October 7-8, 2026, as the official auction of the AACA National Fall Meet. Held at the Hershey Lodge, the sale presents a focused offerings of veteran, Brass Era, and early American automobiles, complemented by a curated selection of rare automobilia. This year’s offering is led by the 1934 Duesenberg Model J Convertible Berline by Murphy, a 1935 Auburn 851 Supercharged Speedster, and a 1915 Mercedes 28/60 HP Town Car and Tourer Display Chassis. Now in its 20th year, the Hershey auction occupies a place in the collector car calendar. title: New study reassesses Herman Cherry's 1970 abstraction and ties to nature
summary: Herman Cherry (1909-1992) was a vital part of the legendary New York School of painters, and like many in his generation, migrated away from figurative expression to abstraction beginning in the mid-1940s. Most writing about Cherry situates him among America’s celebrated abstract and color field artists. Less discussed are the artists—like Mark Tobey and Clyfford Still—whose approach to abstraction never abandoned a representational referent, most especially nature. They embraced what Wassily Kandinsky called “the spirit,” a need to express in color and form one’s inner self, without which there is no art. Equally influential in the years before the Second World War was Los Angeles-based artist and theorist Stanton Macdonald-Wright, who co-conceived Synchromy, a method for using color based on optical and musical principles. title: Parcours des Mondes celebrates 25 years with art spanning continents and centuries in Paris
summary: For six days in September, the narrow streets of Saint-Germain-des-Prés will once again become something between an art fair, an open-air museum and a meeting place for collectors, scholars, dealers and the simply curious. Parcours des Mondes, the international gathering devoted to the arts of Africa, Oceania, Asia and the Americas, as well as archaeology, returns to Paris from September 8 to 13, 2026, this year marking its 25th anniversary. What began 25 years ago as an unusual proposition — bringing these fields together in the galleries of one Paris neighborhood rather than inside a conventional fair hall — has grown into a major annual rendezvous. For the anniversary edition, around fifty resident and international galleries will turn Saint-Germain-des-Prés into a walkable exhibition circuit, with visitors moving from one culture and period to another simply by crossing a street. title: Kunsthalle Recklinghausen opens Villa Romana prize winners exhibition
summary: What Lies Below Is Another Above begins from a simple impossibility: what lies beneath us is never simply below. Every ground is already another surface. Bringing together Villa Romana art prize winners from 2023 to 2025, the exhibition creates an encounter between artistic practices developed independently across different geographies, languages, and political concerns. The works retain the autonomy of their own trajectories while encountering another territory, another institutional history, and another material imagination in Recklinghausen. The Ruhrgebiet offers particularly charged ground for this encounter. Extraction has shaped its landscapes, architectures, economies, and social histories. What happened underground transformed everything above it: cities, infrastructures, forms of labour, migration, bodies, and environments.

title: Madrid's National Archaeological Museum traces the journey from Greek tragedy to Roman comedy
summary: Long before theater became an evening at a playhouse, a Broadway production or a movie adapted for the stage, it was part ritual, part public spectacle and part political instrument. A new presentation at Madrid's National Archaeological Museum looks back at those beginnings, tracing how theater developed from religious celebrations in ancient Greece into one of the most enduring forms of entertainment in the Roman world. Titled “From Greek Tragedy to Roman Comedy: Classical Theater,” the exhibition is the latest installment of the museum's Vitrina Cero program. Drawing on the MAN's bibliographic and archaeological holdings, the display explores not only how Greco-Roman theater developed, but why it mattered — as entertainment, as a way of communicating ideas and, at times, as a tool of political propaganda. title: TarraWarra Museum of Art announces its 2026-27 program
summary: TarraWarra Museum of Art today announces its 2026–27 program, bringing together major exhibitions, new commissions, live music and expanded opportunities to experience the Museum and its Collection. Opening in September 2026, Waterways presents a new rehang of the Collection in the Eva and Marc Besen Centre, accompanied by exclusive Behind the Glass tours. In November 2026, Light Weight explores the material and poetic qualities of light through works from the Collection, a major site-responsive commission and loans from leading Australian contemporary artists. In Autumn 2027, TarraWarra International returns with Under the Same Sky, a major joint exhibition developed with the Jehangir Nicholson Art Foundation at CSMVS, Mumbai, and presented across Australia and India. title: Faro Santander presents its inaugural exhibitions programme
summary: Faro Santander, the new cultural project promoted by the Banco Santander Foundation, opens with an ambitious inaugural exhibitions programme in an evolving cultural hub in Santander, northern Spain. The public opening of Faro Santander completes the revitalisation of one of the most iconic landmarks on Santander’s seafront: the historic Pereda Building, former headquarters of Banco Santander. The transformation of the Pereda Building—a protected cultural heritage asset—has been led by David Chipperfield Architects. Faro Santander’s renovated interior offers more than 10,000 m² of usable floor space across ten levels, of which some 3,000 m² is set aside for galleries spread over five floors. The top two levels are given over to the café-terrace and the restaurant, while three basement levels house an auditorium and building services.

title: The Grolier Club marks 1,000th exhibition with survey of Dieu Donné hand papermaking
summary: The Grolier Club kicks off its 2026–2027 season with the milestone 1,000th exhibition presented at the Club, a new show highlighting revolutions in contemporary American hand papermaking. On view September 8 through November 28, 2026, in the Club’s Ground Floor Gallery, Pioneers in Hand Papermaking: 50 Years of Innovation at Dieu Donné celebrates the 50th anniversary of the Dieu Donné Papermill, a non-profit studio based in the Brooklyn Navy Yard. A leader of the grassroots hand papermaking movement that emerged in the 1970s, Dieu Donné’s master papermakers work with contemporary artists to develop their imagery using the papermaking process. title: October Gallery to present Romuald Hazoumè solo show My Blue Period
summary: October Gallery presents My Blue Period, a solo exhibition by the internationally renowned artist Romuald Hazoumè, which coincides with 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair and Frieze London. Romuald Hazoumè revisits his iconic masques bidons (Fr. bidon – flask, container, bottle)—presenting a striking series of masks made from repurposed plastic containers that are adorned with an eclectic array of found materials. Wittily imagined as portraits of figures inhabiting particular places in the contemporary geo-political landscape, these new sculptures come freighted with Hazoumè’s biting commentaries on current issues of global concern. Displaying a wicked eye for detail, each mask dances before our eyes animated by his irreverent sense of humour. title: transmediale opens call for 2028 festival curator in Berlin
summary: transmediale e.V. is inviting applications for the Festival Curation for transmediale 2028 in Berlin. The festival curator's central responsibility is the development of the curatorial concept and programme for the festival in 2028. The position invites one or more persons with previous curatorial experience to critically engage with topics at the intersection of art, technology, science, society, and politics, and to contribute to transmediale’s 40-year-long history as one of the leading festivals of art and digital culture. Since 2025, transmediale invites a new curator for each edition, bringing their own positionality on the present moment in art and technology. Across editions, this plurality of perspectives is what builds the festival's larger direction over time. title: Esther Schipper now representing Jenny Brosinski
summary: Esther Schipper announced the representation of Jenny Brosinski. Jenny Brosinski was born in Celle, Germany. In 2012 Brosinski completed her Meisterschüler studies at the Weißensee Academy of Art Berlin. She was shortlisted for the Berlin Art Prize in 2014 and in 2024 nominated for the Hans-Purrmann Prize of the City of Speyer. Brosinski currently lives and works in Berlin and Blankensee. Jenny Brosinski’s paintings combine an exploratory approach with a precise sense of composition. On often wide-open fields of unprimed linen or canvas, marks, stains, patches of color and occasional words are set against the exposed surface. Some motifs appear isolated; others form loose constellations or collide with one another. title: Gagosian presents inaugural exhibition of works by Deana Lawson
summary: Gagosian announced its first solo exhibition of works by Deana Lawson. Opening on September 10 at 541 West 24th Street in New York, the exhibition of mirror-framed photographs and holograms engages issues of personhood, surveillance, and control. Lawson debuts selections from Edge Control, a series initiated in 2023 in which she reimagines the monitoring of individuals by beauty supply stores throughout the United States. Recontextualizing surveillance stills taped to windows and entryways, she preserves the ways in which these images warp identity and posit a mode of figuration, intervening only to protect the identities of those pictured. title: Firenze Lai opens first UK exhibition during Frieze London
summary: White Cube Mason’s Yard will present a solo exhibition of new paintings by Firenze Lai (b. 1984, Hong Kong), coinciding with Frieze London 2026. Drawing influence from our ever-increasing time spent online and the continuous development of AI, in her latest works, Lai explores belonging, divisive misinformation, and the impossibility of determining a singular source of truth. Lai was born in Hong Kong in 1984, where she lived and worked for many years before relocating to London in 2022. Growing up in a densely populated metropolis, she was shaped by the frenetic, labyrinthine cityscapes which were formative to the development of her practice. Interrogating the social, political and spatial subtexts that influence individual and collective psyches, her dreamlike paintings of anonymous figures and places reflect upon the human condition.

title: David Kordansky Gallery presents Maia Cruz Palileo's first New York solo exhibition
summary: David Kordansky Gallery will present The World Tangled in You, an exhibition of new paintings by Maia Cruz Palileo and the gallery’s first presentation of Palileo’s work in New York. Featuring both large- and small-scale canvases, the show finds the artist fully engaging with the complex legacies and material possibilities of painting, as well as an increasingly expansive sense of the ways in which family and personal narratives, geopolitical histories, and formal expression intersect. The World Tangled in You is on view in New York at 520 W. 20th St. from September 10 through October 24, 2026. An opening reception will be held on Thursday, September 10, from 6 – 8 PM.
